1. Validate the current bill: confirm meter reads imply 627 kWh (68,865 − 68,238), line items sum to $123.97 ($18.79 + $21.80 + $83.38), and the change versus last month is −$63.42 ($123.97 − $187.39); treat any arithmetic mismatch as a suspected billing error.

2. Map both billing periods to the AEP Ohio tariff: last month (2026-08-10 to 2026-09-09) and current (2026-09-09 to 2026-10-10) both fall under the post-2026-04-10 tariff (fixed $18.788; blended variable rate $0.0347738 + $0.13299 = $0.1677638/kWh for the first 2,000 kWh), so set price_usd = 0.

3. Estimate weather_usd from NOAA degree days: compare last month (CDD 296.5 / HDD 0) to current (CDD 120 / HDD 79), derive a weather-to-kWh coefficient from the bill history, convert the weather-driven kWh difference to dollars at the effective variable rate, or set weather_usd = 0 if no defensible coefficient can be estimated.

4. Compute days_usd for the one-day longer period: value the extra day at last month’s daily average usage (1,005 kWh ÷ 30 days) times the effective variable rate.

5. Compute usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly −$63.42; verify the tariff-modeled current-period total matches $123.97 within rounding, otherwise set billing_error_suspected = true and billing_error_usd to the discrepancy.

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
